title: Interoceptive loops close the circuit
objective: Explain how interoceptive afferents complete organ-regulating loops, linking the tracks.

steps.title: Sensing is half the loop
steps.body: Every homeostatic reflex needs an afferent limb — the sensor. **[[interoception|Interoceptive]]** afferents (spinal/[[DRG]] and vagal/[[nodose ganglion|nodose]]) are that limb for the viscera. Without them, the brain loses its direct neural readout of the organ, and neural reflexes can't close the loop.

steps.prompt: Why are visceral afferents essential to organ reflexes?
options: They form the afferent limb; the brain can't regulate what it can't sense
They act as the effector that physically moves and contracts the organ
They completely replace hormonal control of the organ all by themselves
They only matter during early development, never in the adult animal
steps.explanation: Regulation needs sensing. Visceral afferents report the organ's state so a reflex (or the brain) can respond — the input side of control.

variants.setup: You remove the sensory (afferent) limb of an organ reflex.
options: It can no longer sense the variable, so regulation fails
Nothing changes, since the effector limb is still intact
The loop flips into positive feedback and runs away
variants.reveal: With no afferent limb the loop is blind and can't correct — regulation fails.

steps.prompt: The vagal 'inflammatory reflex' (Track B) is an example of what?
options: An interoceptive reflex: afferents sense inflammation and efferents dampen it
A purely hormonal loop: cytokines alone shut inflammation off
A somatic stretch reflex, much like the familiar knee-jerk
A positive-feedback loop: vagal output amplifies inflammation
steps.explanation: It's a reflex arc where afferents sense immune signals and efferent [[vagus|vagal]] output modulates inflammation — sensing and response, closing the loop.

variants.setup: Afferents detect inflammation and vagal output then dampens it.
variants.reveal: Sensing inflammation and responding via the vagus is an interoceptive reflex arc.

steps.title: Why it all connects
steps.body: Sensory biology (A), neuroimmune loops (B), the tools (C), and this anatomy/physiology (D) all meet here: visceral afferents are the afferent limb of the loops that keep organs healthy — and the exact neurons the lab, and your project, aim to understand.

sources.note: Spinal sensory innervation of the intestine; interoceptive control of visceral organs.
